concepts.def: Varieties of Religious Experience; four marks: ineffability, noetic quality, transiency, passivity; pragmatic test.
Idea of the Holy; mysterium tremendum et fascinans; non-rational core of religion; awe and attraction.
Religion as feeling of absolute dependence; Speeches on Religion; foundation of liberal Protestantism.
Sudden religious change; St Paul on Damascus Road (Acts 9); Augustine in garden; James studied as type.
Union with divine; Christian (Teresa of Avila), Sufi (Rumi), Hindu (Ramakrishna); often via contemplative practice.
Principle of Credulity (trust experience absent reason not to); Principle of Testimony (trust others' reports).

Religious & Ethical Teachings about Medical Ethics — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religious & Ethical Teachings about Medical Ethics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.
